report:
I found nothing that would block this merge. All four pages are there, they share a nav, and the site has no external requests and no build step.

**Checks run**
- **Tests:** `NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) node --test tests/*.test.js` and `npm test` both report `# tests 50 … # pass 50 # fail 0`.
- **Formatting:** `npx --no-install prettier --check .` reports "All matched files use Prettier code style!". The repo has no lint config to break.
- **Layout at 360px:** I opened each page in headless Chrome at 360px over `file://` (no server, as the README describes) and opened the mobile menu. Every page gave `scrollWidth == innerWidth == 360`, with no element past the right edge and no console errors.
- **Genre filter edge cases:** all behaved correctly.
  - Clicking "Poetry (3)" gives `?genre=poetry` and "Showing 3 books in Poetry".
  - Back gives `books.html` and "Showing all 15 books".
  - `?genre=%20Science%20fiction%20` is rewritten to `?genre=science-fiction` and shows 3 books.
  - `?genre=bogus` falls back to all 15.
- **Code read-through:** the contact form validates with inline errors, `aria-invalid` and a summary, moves focus to the first invalid field, and replaces the demo message rather than adding another. The nav has a skip link, `aria-current`, an `aria-expanded` toggle and Escape to close. Headings are in order, tap targets are at least 44px, and reduced motion is respected. The tests only check event logic against fixed dates, so they won't break as the calendar moves on.
- **Git state:** `git status` is unchanged; all 14 files are still staged as new.

**Nits (not blocking)**
- The README says `npm test` still needs `NODE_PATH` set. That is true only when `NODE_PATH` isn't already set: this environment exports it, and `npm test` passed without it being set by hand.
- `js/events.js` has a past event ("Harvest Poetry Night", 2026-10-10) that never displays. The last event is on 2027-01-16, so from then on the Events page will only show the "no upcoming events" message.
- `updateSummary` in `js/visit.js` rewrites the `role="alert"` summary on every keystroke while a field is invalid, so some screen readers may announce it again even when the text hasn't changed.
- On a selected genre pill, the radio's burgundy accent colour (`accent-color: var(--burgundy)`) sits on the dark `--ink` background with little contrast. The pill's own colour change still shows which genre is selected.
